The Jurassic Coast by Motorcycle

Dorset's Jurassic Coast is a UNESCO World Heritage Site stretching 95 miles from Orcombe Point in Devon to Old Harry Rocks in Dorset. It exposes 185 million years of geological history in dramatic coastal cliffs, arches, and coves. For motorcyclists, the roads along this coastline combine beautiful riding with world-class scenery.

The Route (90 miles)

Start in Lyme Regis and head east along the coast through West Bay, Abbotsbury, and Weymouth to Lulworth Cove and Durdle Door, finishing at Swanage or Studland.

Key Stops

  • Lyme Regis: The fossil capital of Britain. Walk the Cobb harbour wall and hunt for fossils on the beach.
  • West Bay: The dramatic sandstone cliffs made famous by the TV series Broadchurch. The harbour is a pleasant stop.
  • Chesil Beach: An 18-mile natural shingle bank. The B3157 runs along the top with views across the Fleet Lagoon.
  • Durdle Door: The iconic limestone arch. A short walk from the clifftop car park (which has motorcycle parking).
  • Lulworth Cove: A near-perfect circular cove carved by the sea. Geological interpretation centre and good café.
  • Kimmeridge Bay: Dark shale beaches and fossil hunting. The approach road through the Purbeck Hills is excellent riding.
  • Old Harry Rocks: Chalk stacks at the eastern end of the Jurassic Coast. Walk from Studland car park.
The Jurassic Coast is best ridden from west to east — the sun is behind you in the morning and the light improves as the day progresses. The geology changes from older Triassic rocks in the west to younger Cretaceous chalk in the east.

Riding Character

The coastal roads are a mix of flowing A-roads and narrow B-roads. The B3157 from Abbotsbury to Bridport is particularly enjoyable — sweeping bends with sea views. The Purbeck Hills section around Corfe Castle and Kimmeridge adds inland variety with dramatic views back to the coast.

Combining with Other Rides

  • Extend west into Devon for the Exe Estuary and Sidmouth coast
  • Head inland to the Dorset Downs for quiet rolling roads
  • Visit Corfe Castle — the dramatic ruin is visible from the A351 and the village is charming

Accommodation and Dining

Lyme Regis, Weymouth, and Swanage all make excellent overnight stops along the Jurassic Coast route. The Seaside Boarding House in Burton Bradstock combines boutique comfort with a spectacular cliff-top location overlooking Chesil Beach and the open sea beyond. For camping, several sites along the coast offer pitches with sea views at reasonable prices during the touring season.

The Anchor Inn at Seatown serves fresh Dorset seafood with uninterrupted views across Lyme Bay — one of the finest pub locations anywhere on the south coast of England. West Bay's harbour area has excellent fish and chip shops that have served generations of visitors. The Hive Beach Café at Burton Bradstock serves locally caught crab and mackerel dishes that touring riders consistently rate among the best seaside food in southern England. Plan your riding around lunch stops at these establishments and you'll discover that the Jurassic Coast is as rewarding for its gastronomy as it is for its geological drama and scenic coastal roads.
keyTakeaways: The Jurassic Coast is a UNESCO World Heritage Site running 95 miles from Orcombe Point in Devon to Old Harry Rocks in Dorset.
The 90-mile route runs Lyme Regis east through West Bay, Abbotsbury and Weymouth to Lulworth Cove and Durdle Door.
Ride west to east so the sun is behind you in the morning and the light improves through the day.
The B3157 from Abbotsbury to Bridport is the riding highlight, with sweeping bends and sea views.
Durdle Door and Old Harry Rocks are short walks from clifftop car parks, with motorcycle parking at Durdle Door.

faq.q: Which direction should I ride the coast?
faq.a: Ride west to east, starting at Lyme Regis. The sun sits behind you in the morning and the light improves as the day progresses. The geology also tells a story in this direction, changing from older Triassic rocks in the west to younger Cretaceous chalk in the east. Finishing at Swanage or Studland near Old Harry Rocks makes a natural end point.

faq.q: Where can I park the bike for Durdle Door?
faq.a: Durdle Door is reached by a short walk from the clifftop car park, which has motorcycle parking. Lulworth Cove nearby has its own car park, cafe and geology interpretation centre. For Old Harry Rocks at the eastern end, park at Studland and walk out to the chalk stacks. These clifftop car parks are the practical bases for the coast's most famous viewpoints.

faq.q: What is the riding like along the route?
faq.a: The coastal roads mix flowing A-roads with narrow B-roads. The B3157 from Abbotsbury to Bridport is the standout, with sweeping bends and sea views across Lyme Bay. The Purbeck Hills around Corfe Castle and Kimmeridge add inland variety and dramatic views back to the coast. It is enjoyable rather than demanding riding, well suited to a relaxed touring pace.

faq.q: How long does the ride take?
faq.a: The core route is about 90 miles from Lyme Regis to Swanage, which is easily a full day once you factor in stops at fossil beaches, Durdle Door, Lulworth Cove and the various cafes. Allow time to walk to the main viewpoints. You can extend west into Devon for the Exe Estuary and Sidmouth, or inland to the quiet Dorset Downs.
